rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an was sent to Muhammad in truth, confirms what came before it, and continues the guidance previously given through the Torah and Gospel.
rows.anchor: hakk u hakikati müştemil ve önündekileri musaddık olmak üzere cereyân-ı hakka göre peyderpey indirmektedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier books promised a great future prophet; the Qur'an's arrival validates those prophecies as revelation, whereas without it they would be empty promises.
rows.anchor: kütüb-i sâlife ve enbiyâ-yı mâziye istikbalde büyük bir peygamberin kudûmünü vaad ederek hidâyet ve irşadlarını böyle bir gāye-i kemâle tevcih etmiş olduklarından

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By confirming Muhammad, the Qur'an also confirms earlier prophets and establishes mutual testimony among the revealed books, with the final Prophet heading them.
rows.anchor: bütün enbiyâ-yı sâlifenin risaletlerini de tasdik ve isbat eden bir Furkān-ı mübîn olmuş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an renews the earlier books' enduring principles while revising subsidiary rulings for the circumstances and welfare of different times, places, and communities.
rows.anchor: mesâlih-i lâikalarına müte‘allik ahkâm ve şerâyi‘-i fer‘iyelerini ta‘dîl ü tecdîd ederek dîn-i hakkı cemî‘-i ezmân ve emkinede

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier scriptures and laws can be accepted as true only when Allah and His Messenger confirm them, as the legal maxim states.
rows.anchor: Bu mâna usûl-i fıkıhta şu kā‘ide-i teşrî‘ile ifade olunur: “Bizden evvelkilerin şeriatları bizim de şeriatımızdır. Fakat Allah ve Resûlü tarafından tasdîkan nakledilmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the Furqan, God distinguishes truth from falsehood and good from evil, establishes their paths and laws, and assigns their outcomes under His will.
rows.anchor: alâmetler, deliller, âyetler de ikāme eylemiş, her birinin hükmünü, netîce-i lâzimesini başka başka yapmış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who reject God's signs that distinguish and guide to truth, especially by attacking divine unity or the prophets, are condemned to severe punishment.
rows.anchor: tarîk-i hakkı gösterir aklî ve naklî âyât ü delâil-i ilâhiyeye küfr eden ve ale’l-husûs Allah teâlâ’nın vahdâniyetine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is invincible and beyond humiliation; He may forbear for a time, but ultimately overwhelms those who try to abase the truth and punishes their false course.
rows.anchor: Allah şâibe-i zilletten münezzeh öyle yenilmez bir Azîz’dir ki dehşetli bir intikamı vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Izzet is the complete opposite of humiliation, while intiqam derives from requital that turns a criminal's pleasure in wrongdoing into the pain of punishment.
rows.anchor: “İzzet”, “zillet”in zıdd-ı tâmmı, “intikam” da “nimet”in zıddı “nikmet”ten me’huz olup ibrâz-ı satvet etmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forgives those who repent and return to faith, but forgiveness is good only when it does not blur right and wrong or encourage continued evil.
rows.anchor: hakk u nâhakkı teşviş etmek, hasenât ü seyyiâtı müsâvî tutmak gibi bir şerr-i küllîye sebep olmaması ile meşruttur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forbearance without a force that protects its purity is not good; an Arab poet's verse expressing this was approved by the Prophet.
rows.anchor: tasvîb-i Resûlullah’a mazhar olmuştu: وَلاَ خَيْرَ فِي حِلْمٍ إِذَا لَمْ يَكُنْ لَه بَوَادِرُ تَحْمِي صَفْوَهُ أَنْ يُكَدَّرَا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet's image means that a restraint without impulses to protect its serenity from being clouded has no merit.
rows.anchor: yoksa o hilimde hayr yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love of truth and good rises in proportion to hatred of evil and falsehood.
rows.anchor: Hakk u hayra mahabbetin derecesi şerr ü bâtıla buğz u adavetin derecesiyle mütenâsibdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness has value only for one able to punish; calling incapacity forgiveness is ridiculous, and the ability to forgive entails the ability to retaliate.
rows.anchor: Cürme mücâzat edebilmek kudreti mutasavver olmayan bir âciz-i mutlakın “affettim” demesi pek gülünç olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God, the living sustainer, protects good and guidance through mercy and removes evil and treachery through might and retribution, making Him the true deity and refuge of hope.
rows.anchor: hayr u hidayeti rahmetiyle himâye, şerr ü hıyaneti de izzet ü intikamıyla izâle eder bir Hayy ü Kayyûm

rows.speaker: bazı kimseler
rows.claim: Some people say they do not want a deity capable of retribution against evil and instead want a helpless, comforting object of devotion.
rows.anchor: “Biz şerre karşı intikama kādir mâbud istemeyiz” diye hakka küfr

rows.speaker: Nasârâ
rows.claim: Elmalılı describes Christians as treating Jesus, Mary, and God as a vulnerable family whose sacrifice redeems inherited sin, while construing one deity as three persons and simultaneously mortal and eternal, weak and powerful.
rows.anchor: sonraki Nasârâ da Hazret-i Îsâ’yı böyle bir bebek, validesi Hazret-i Meryem’i böyle bir mahbûbe, Cenâb-ı Allah’ı da berhayat olduğu müddetçe

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects this Trinity as contradictory: it makes the deity at once existent and absent, mortal and eternal, powerless and powerful, one and three.
rows.anchor: bir var aynı zamanda yok, fâni aynı zamanda bâkī, âciz aynı zamanda kādir, bir aynı zamanda üç ve üç aynı zamanda bir mâbud

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He argues that the doctrine treats sin as inevitable and punishment as unavoidable, then removes the punishing authority so people can sin while transferring the penalty to another; this negates the deity.
rows.anchor: İşte teslîs-i Nasârâ’nın bütün meâli böyle bir nefy-i ma‘bud muammâsıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus never invited people to this doctrine; his miraculous works attest his prophethood, and people should follow his teaching as the first Christians did and affirm divine unity.
rows.anchor: ilk Nasârâ’nın yaptıkları gibi ta‘lîmât-ı Îsâ’ya ittibâ‘edilecek ve tevhîd-i ilâhî üzere yürünecek yerde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı traces the corruption of Christianity to secret societies, early distortions in Gospel translations, and eventually the Council of Nicaea.
rows.anchor: bunun mebde’i cem‘iyyât-ı[^17] sırriyeye ve ilk İncil tercemelerindeki tahrîfât-ı evveliyeye ve ba‘dehu[^18] İznik sinoduna müntehî olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says Christians give little weight to Gospel wording, claiming to promote its spirit while continually revising and replacing its copies.
rows.anchor: Nasârâ İncil’in nusûsuna ehemmiyet vermezler de rûhunu tervic ediyoruz diye İncil nüshalarını her zaman tecdid ve tebdil ederler

rows.speaker: Avrupa tarih felsefeleri
rows.claim: European philosophies of history hold that the doctrine of creation from nothing entered philosophy through Christianity.
rows.anchor: Avrupa tarih felsefeleri bu akidenin felsefeye ancak Nasrâniyet’ten girmiş olduğu fikrindedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All revealed religions affirm that God is the first cause and creator who brings the universe into being from nothing, without needing matter.
rows.anchor: kâffe-i edyân-ı semâviyenin ittifak ettikleri bir hakikat vardır ki o da illet-i ûlâ olan Allah teâlâ’nın Hâlık olması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ordinary generation can occur in created causes, but true causation is creation from nothing; making God a begetter conflicts with this distinction.
rows.anchor: Tevlid nazariyesi mebde’inde bir tenakuzdan kurtulmak ihtimali bulunmayan bir nazariyedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Gospel's ambiguous term for God as Father means Creator and Maker, not biological parent.
rows.anchor: “Hâlık-ı Rahîm” mânasını ifade eden اب ta‘bîr-i müteşâbihinin والد mânasıyla tevili

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus' use of Father means my merciful Creator; the wording is also a particular divine kindness toward Jesus, whom opponents accused of being fatherless.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Îsâ’nın “Babam” dediği zaman “Rahîm olan Hâlıkım” demiş olduğunda da şüphe yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı rejects Church fathers' literal interpretation of Father as parent because it contradicts the belief that God creates.
rows.anchor: hakīkat-i lügaviyesi olan وَالِد mânasına haml etmeye çalışmaları da halk akidesiyle telifi kābil olmayan bir tenakuzdur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an summarizes Christian errors about God and scripture as disbelief in divine signs, preserving its dignified moral style while extending the admonition, then warns of severe punishment.
rows.anchor: ahlâk-ı Kur’âniyenin nezâhet ve vakarıyla kābil-i te’lîf olmayacağını tefhim

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's Furqan announces the certain defeat of those who dare to abase the truth.
rows.anchor: hakkı tezlîle cür’et edenlerin âkıbet mağlûbiyyet-i kat‘iyyelerini ilan eden bir furkān-ı ilâhîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine retribution is wise and just, grounded in infinite knowledge, power, and will rather than base, ignorant vengeance.
rows.anchor: ‘ayn-ı hikmet ve hakk-ı izzet olan ve nâmütenahî bir ilm ü kudret ve iradenin muktezası bulunan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing in heaven or earth, whether particular or universal, material or spiritual, inward or outward, is hidden from God; all is known to Him.
rows.anchor: cüz’î küllî, maddî mânevî, enfüsî âfâkī hiçbir şey Allah’a gizli kalmaz, hepsi O’nun mâlûmudur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For God, the existence of anything in itself and in any state is identical with knowledge.
rows.anchor: bir tavırda mevcûdiyeti Allah’a nazaran ‘ayn-ı ilimdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine knowledge is eternal and the basis of existence, unlike the newly acquired, representational, or shadow-like knowledge of human beings.
rows.anchor: İlm-i ilâhî beşerde olduğu gibi temessülî, tasavvurî, zıllî bir ilm-i hâdis değil, mebnâ-yı vücud olan bir ilm-i ezelîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forms people in the womb as He wills, choosing their form and developing their material through successive stages of growth and differentiation.
rows.anchor: nasıl dilerse öylece tasvir eder. Hangi surete isterse ona kor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God composes human organs, tissues, vessels, nerves, senses, and functions into a living person, who may be complete or incomplete, male, female, or intersex.
rows.anchor: tam veya nâkıs, erkek veya dişi veya hunsâ, canlı bir nefis suretine ifrağ eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Across each stage God adds a new act of creation and transforms and refines humans from one form and quality to another.
rows.anchor: her tavırda bir halk-ı cedîd ilâve ederek suretten surete

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human formation involves familiar sciences and hidden divine sciences, all applied beyond human observation while people are absent from the womb.
rows.anchor: perde-i hafâda bulunan nice ulûm-i ledünniyenin de alâkası bulunduğunu ve sonra bütün bunların sizin gıyâbınızda tatbik edildiğini

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Womb formation combines shared traits linking humanity back to Adam and creation with unique qualities that distinguish each individual.
rows.anchor: ta‘ayyün-i şahsî ve temâyüz-i ferdîyi ifade eden ve bir ikincisi bulunmayan suver u keyfiyyât-ı mahsûsa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus too was formed in a womb and is one of God's creatures, so God should be understood first as the Creator who formed Jesus and every person.
rows.anchor: Îsâ dahi onun böyle erhâmda tasvir ettiği sizlerden birisidir, O’nun bir mahlûkudur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflection on human formation shows that God knows the unseen and visible, has complete power and will, and is not subject to any external necessity.
rows.anchor: O’na gayb u şehadet mâlumdur. Kudret-i bâliğası vardır, aczden münezzehtir, irade ve meşîeti vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has a comprehensive knowledge preceding events, so no hidden or absent matter, including shirk concealed as a mystery, escapes Him.
rows.anchor: hâdisâta tekaddüm eden bir ilm-i muhît-i muhkemi vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Presence and absence are relative to created, changing knowledge; God creates knowers, known things, faculties, wills, and acts, linking them in an order that guides them toward their ends.
rows.anchor: ilimler, mâlumlar, gözler, gönüller, akıllar, kalbler, iradeler, fiiller yaratan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God is neither blind nor ignorant, prophets' reports of unseen matters such as the coming of the Furqan are knowledge He taught them.
rows.anchor: haber vermesi ise bunların hepsi onun i‘lâm[^36] u ta‘lîmidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's independent, complete power encompasses every existing and possible thing, from particles and bodies to material and spiritual realities, all of which are subject to Him.
rows.anchor: maddiyyât u ma‘neviyyâtıyla hep O’ndandır ve O’na musahhardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nature and its laws are effects of divine power, not masters of it: natural processes are repeated regular effects, while miracles are singular irregular effects.
rows.anchor: Tabiat O’nun te’sîrât-ı mütekerrire ve muttaridesi, hilâf-ı tabiat hârikalar da O’nun te’sîrât-ı münferide ve gayr-i muttaridesidir
